channel.title: Entuned Blog | Retail Music Strategy
channel.description: Research-backed insights on retail music strategy, in-store customer behavior, and AI-powered audio optimization.

item.title: What's the Best BPM for Workout Music? What the Research Actually Says
item.description: The research on music tempo and exercise: the 125-140 BPM band, the ~140 ceiling, and why the beat itself — not the hype — does most of the work.

item.title: What Music Tempo Should a Coffee Shop Play? The Honest Answer
item.description: Slow music slows customers down — but the famous spend lift came from a restaurant bar, not a café. What the tempo research really says for a coffee shop.

item.title: Calming Music for a Dog Grooming Salon: What the Research Actually Says
item.description: Research shows the right music lowers stress in dogs — but they tune a static loop out within days. What that means for grooming salons.

item.title: How Do Retail Music Services Actually Work?
item.description: Retail music services range from basic licensed playlists to adaptive, generative platforms that adjust in real time. The difference matters: a 1982 study...

item.title: The Science of Store Music: How Sound Quietly Changes What People Buy
item.description: What the research really says about store music: the effects are real but small and depend on fit. A meta-analysis of 32 studies, and what it means for your store.

item.title: What Music Should a Bar Play? Why the Volume Matters More Than the Song
item.description: In a field experiment, a bar's music volume measurably changed the pace of the room. The sound level, not the song, sets your bar's energy — worth setting on purpose.

item.title: What Music Should a Bookshop Play? The Research Is Counterintuitive
item.description: What the research says about music and browsing in a bookshop: it can change how long people stay, what they pick up, or neither — so you have to choose the outcome.

item.title: What Music Should a Clothing Store Play? Why Letting Staff Pick Cost One Brand 11%
item.description: When one fashion brand let staff pick the music, sales fell up to 11%. Your store's music is a brand signal — and letting it drift has a measured cost.

item.title: What Music Should a Flower Shop Play? There's Actually a Study
item.description: A field experiment in an actual florist found romantic music lifted spending — and ordinary pop did nothing. The lever is fit, not just nice music.

item.title: What Music Should a Hotel Lobby Play? It's the Brand's First Sentence
item.description: A lobby is the brand's first sentence. Research on servicescape and atmosphere shows music sets perceived quality and sophistication the moment a guest arrives.

item.title: What Music Should a Jewelry Store Play? What the Research Suggests
item.description: There's no jewelry-store study — but the closest research is a clean match: upscale music nudges shoppers toward the premium choice without anyone noticing.

item.title: What Music Should a Restaurant Play? It Changes How the Food Tastes
item.description: Sound changes how food tastes and what diners choose. The research on sonic seasoning, volume, and the slow-tempo lever that pours more drinks.

item.title: What Music Should a Supermarket Play? When It's Crowded, Speed Up
item.description: The rule says slow music makes shoppers spend more. In a crowded supermarket it flips: fast music lifts spending, across 43,676 baskets. Here's why.

item.title: What Should Retailers Look for in a Music Provider?

item.title: Your Store Music Has a Second Audience: Your Staff
item.description: Your in-store music has a second audience: the people who work in it all day. The research on how it helps — or quietly grates on — your staff.

item.title: How to Choose a Music Service for Your Store
item.description: How to choose a music service for your retail store. What to evaluate — licensing, contracts, measurement — and how Mood Media, Soundtrack, and Entuned compare.

item.title: How Much Does a BMI Music License Cost? (And How to Avoid It)
item.description: BMI fees for a small business run roughly $300 to $600 per year (publicly reported) — but BMI is one of four PROs. Licensing all of them directly runs about $1,300 to $1,500+ a year.
